title: Data Preparation
text:
Y <- read.table('data.txt', header = TRUE) %>%
  select(strain, environ, yield, protein, oil)

IDs <- Y$strain
uIDs <- unique(IDs)

env <- Y$environ
uenv <- unique(env)

CV1: To predict untested genotypes in observed environments.

folds <- 5

fold <- rep(1:folds, each = ceiling(length(uIDs) / folds))[order(runif(length(uIDs)))]

Y$CV1 <- NA

for(i in 1:folds) {
  tmp <- IDs %in% uIDs[fold == i]
  Y$CV1[tmp] <- i
}

table(Y$CV1)

CV2: To predict tested genotypes in observed environments.

folds <- 5

Y$CV2 <- NA

for(i in uIDs) {
  tmp <- which(IDs == i)
  ni  <- length(tmp)
  fold <- sample(1:folds, size = ni, replace = ni > folds)
  Y$CV2[tmp] <- fold
}

table(Y$CV2)

CV0: To predict tested genotypes in unobserved environments.

folds_env <- length(uenv)

fold <- sample(1:folds_env, size = folds_env)

Y$CV0 <- NA

for(i in 1:folds_env) {
  tmp <- env %in% uenv[fold == i]
  Y$CV0[tmp] <- i
}

table(Y$CV0)


writexl::write_xlsx(Y, "Y_CV.xlsx")

The saved file was used for hyperparameter tuning. The same code was then rerun with different random seeds to test the models under five independent data partitions for CV1 and CV2.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Environment

env <- read.table('data.txt', header = TRUE) %>% pull(environ)

env <- factor(env, levels = unique(env))

Fixed effect - Incidence matrix

EZ <- as.matrix(model.matrix(~env - 1))

rownames(EZ) <- 1:length(env)

colnames(EZ) <- levels(env)

save(EZ, file = 'EZ.rda') 

Random effect (for interaction GxE)

E <- EZ %*% t(EZ)

rownames(E) <- 1:nrow(EZ)

colnames(E) <- 1:nrow(EZ)

save(E, file = 'E.rda')

title: Data Preparation
text:
G matrix
The genomic relationship matrix represent genetic similarity among individuals based on genome-wide molecular markers.
Genotypes x Markers

SNPs <- as.matrix(read.table("gen.txt", h = T, sep = "," ))

The G matrix provided from non linear kernels build here, show the best hyperparameters after tunning.
To optimizing the computational process, we decomposed the G matrix of all models to avoid recalculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors at each MCMC iteration.

GBLUP
Genotypes x Genotypes

library(AGHmatrix)

Gn <- Gmatrix(SNPmatrix = SNPs, maf = 0.05, missingValue = -9, method = "VanRaden")

Fixed effect - Incidence matrix

IDs <- read.table('data.txt', header = TRUE) %>% pull(strain)

IDs <- factor(IDs, levels = rownames(Gn))

GZ <- as.matrix(model.matrix(~IDs - 1))

Random effect - Observations × Observations

G <- GZ %*% Gn %*% t(GZ)

save(G, file = 'G.rda') # For GxE interaction

GDec <- eigen(G)

rownames(GDec$vectors) <- rownames(G)

save(GDec, file = 'GDec.rda')

title: Main effects models
text:
CV1

folds  <- 1:5


Yield

yield <- Y$yield
env <- Y$environ
uenv <- unique(env)

set.seed(1)

ETA <- list(
  list(X = EZ, model = "FIXED"),
  list(V = GDec$vectors, d = GDec$values, model = "RKHS")
)

list_metrics <- list()

for (fold in folds) {
  
  cat("  Processing Fold", fold, "\n")
  
  testing <- which(Y$CV1 == fold)

  yNA <- yield
  yNA[testing] <- NA
  
  fm <- BGLR(
    y = yNA,
    ETA = ETA,
    nIter = nIter,
    burnIn = burnIn,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  yHat <- fm$yHat
  
  for (a in uenv) {
    
    idx_env  <- which(env == a)
    join <- intersect(idx_env, testing)
    
    if (length(join) > 1) {
      
      cor_val <- cor(yHat[join], yield[join])
      
      list_metrics[[length(list_metrics) + 1]] <-
        data.frame(
          Fold = fold,
          Environment = a,
          Predictive_Capacity = cor_val
        )
    }
  }
}

df_metricas <- do.call(rbind, list_metrics)

df_metrics <- bind_rows(list_metrics) %>% 
  group_by(Environment) %>% 
  summarise(pred = mean(Predictive_Capacity), sd = sd(Predictive_Capacity), .groups = "drop")

  cat("\n Fold Processing", f, "\n")

    burnIn = 5000, 
    thin = 10,

  )

  predict_list[[f]] <- data.frame(
    Fold = f,
    Genotype = idx_test,
    Observed = y[idx_test],
    Predicted = yhat_test
  )

  predict_list <- list()
  
  for (f in 1:5) {
    
    cat("  Fold", f, "\n")
    
    idx_test <- which(folds == f)

      ETA = ETA,

      burnIn = 5000,
      thin = 10,

      Genotype = idx_test,

title: Random Forest
text:
CV1

folds  <- 1:5


Yield

yield <- Y$yield
env <- Y$environ
IDs <- Y$strain
uenv <- unique(env)

X_markers <- SNPs[IDs, ]

data_rf <- data.frame(
  yield = yield,
  environ = as.factor(env),
  X_markers,
  check.names = FALSE
)

colnames(data_rf) <- make.names(colnames(data_rf))

set.seed(1)

metric_list <- list()

for (fold in folds) {
  
  cat("  Fold Processing", fold, "\n")
  
  testing <- which(Y$CV1 == fold)
  training <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(Y)), testing)
  
  rf_fit <- ranger(
    yield ~ .,
    data = data_rf[training, ],
    num.trees = 500,
    importance = "none"
  )
  
  yHat <- rep(NA, length(yield))
  yHat[testing] <- predict(
    rf_fit,
    data = data_rf[testing, ]
  )$predictions
  
  for (a in uenv) {
    
    idx_env <- which(env == a)
    set <- intersect(idx_env, testing)
    
    if (length(set) > 1) {
      
      cor_val <- cor(yHat[set], yield[set],
                     use = "complete.obs")
      
      metric_list[[length(metric_list) + 1]] <-
        data.frame(
          Fold = fold,
          Environment = a,
          Predictive_Capacity = cor_val
        )
    }
  }
}

df_metricas <- bind_rows(metric_list)

df_metrics <- df_metricas %>%
  group_by(Environment) %>%
  summarise(
    pred = mean(Predictive_Capacity),
    sd = sd(Predictive_Capacity),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

CV1

folds  <- 1:5


Yield

yield <- Y$yield
env <- Y$environ
uenv <- unique(env)

set.seed(1)

ETA <- list(
  list(X = EZ, model = "FIXED"),
  list(V = GDec$vectors, d = GDec$values, model = "RKHS"),
  list(V = GxEDec$vectors, d = GxEDec$values, model = "RKHS")
)

list_metrics <- list()

for (fold in folds) {
  
  cat("  Processing Fold", fold, "\n")
  
  testing <- which(Y$CV1 == fold)

  yNA <- yield
  yNA[testing] <- NA
  
  fm <- BGLR(
    y = yNA,
    ETA = ETA,
    nIter = nIter,
    burnIn = burnIn,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  yHat <- fm$yHat
  
  for (a in uenv) {
    
    idx_env  <- which(env == a)
    conjunto <- intersect(idx_env, testing)
    
    if (length(conjunto) > 1) {
      
      cor_val <- cor(yHat[conjunto], yield[conjunto])
      
      list_metrics[[length(list_metrics) + 1]] <-
        data.frame(
          Fold = fold,
          Environment = a,
          Predictive_Capacity = cor_val
        )
    }
  }
}

df_metricas <- do.call(rbind, list_metrics)

df_metrics <- bind_rows(list_metrics) %>% 
  group_by(Environment) %>% 
  summarise(pred = mean(Predictive_Capacity), sd = sd(Predictive_Capacity), .groups = "drop")

writexl::write_xlsx(df_metrics, "GBLUP_CV1_Yield_GxE.xlsx")

title: Introduction
text:
This repository contains all the scripts and documentation to reproduce the analysis of the paper Non-linear Kernel Methods for Genomic Prediction of Soybean Yield and Quality in Multi-Environment Trials.
Authors:
Wanessa Alves Lima Paiva
Weverton Gomes da Costa
Leandro Pacheco Machado
Ana Carolina Campana Nascimento
Diego Jarquin
Moyses Nascimento
Abstract:
Soybean key traits such as Grain Yield, Protein content, and Oil content exhibit strong non-linear effects, including epistasis and genotype-by-environment interactions (GEI). Hence, making kernel-based genomic prediction (GP) models ideal candidates to be more effective than linear conventional approaches like Genomic Best Linear Unbiased Predictor (GBLUP). In this study, we analyzed Grain Yield and seed quality in SoyNAM dataset, composed of 1,379 genotypes evaluated across six environments, to compare non-linear kernel methods (Laplacian, Gaussian, Bessel, and Polynomial) to the GBLUP model. Considering two variance structures, main effects only and main and interaction effects, we evaluated the predictive ability of models under three cross-validation scenarios: CV1, predicting untested genotypes in observed environments; CV2, predicting tested genotypes in observed environments; and CV0, predicting tested genotypes in novel environments. We also compared the models with Random Forest and evaluated the same models on an additional dataset containing traits with epistatic effects.
The datasets provided from: Ray, Jarquin and Howard (2023) and Costa et al. (2026).
The codes are organized in the following tabs:
- Data Preparation: script to build genomic matrices and cross validation scenarios.
- Hyperparameter Tuning: script to tune the hyperparameters of non linear kernels.
- Variance Components: script to estimate variance components of the models.
- Models: scripts to fit models under two frameworks:

Main effects
Main and interaction effects

- Random Forest: scripts to fit Random Forest.
- Additional Dataset: scripts to fit models under epistasis dataset.

  for (fold in folds) {
    
    cat("  Processing Fold", fold, "\n")
    
    # Test fold indices
